video_title: Blake Griffin Talks Being a ‘Clipper For Life,’ The Final Injury & Life After Basketball

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on the challenges of early NBA success
quotes.excerpt: I didn't know what I was doing. I can't believe people were entrusting me with having a house.
quotes.quote: It's funny being 37 now, looking back at that time and being like, man, I didn't know what I was doing. I can't believe people were entrusting me with having a house, a car, and doing all these adult things. I wasn't an adult yet.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his early NBA days: I was 37 looking back and thinking man I did not know what I was doing. I can not believe people were entrusting me with having a house and doing all these adult things. I was not an adult yet.

quotes.excerpt: He made several racist remarks and also had a history of doing a lot of things.
quotes.quote: He made several racist remarks and also had a history of doing a lot of things that were really shitty.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin reflects on the Donald Sterling era with the Clippers: He made several racist remarks and also had a history of doing a lot of things that were really shitty.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on his future involvement in basketball
quotes.excerpt: I don't have a clear-cut plan, but I'm 90% sure I won't be involved in basketball.
quotes.quote: I don't have a clear-cut plan, but I'm 90% sure I won't be involved in basketball. I'll obviously be supportive and help out there, but I don't want to stay in the NBA world or anything like that. I think once I'm done, I'll be done.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his post-playing career: I am 90 percent sure I will not be involved in basketball. I do not want to stay in the NBA world or anything like that. I think once I am done I will be done.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on the negativity surrounding player scrutiny
quotes.excerpt: I don't need to go on TV and tell everybody that the guy who went three for
quotes.quote: I always thought that there was a little bit too much negativity when it came to scrutinizing players. This is a job that 400 something guys have. It's extremely hard. I don't need to go on TV and tell everybody that the guy who went three for 17 sucks at basketball. He doesn't. He had an off night. Instead, maybe I can walk you through some of the things he maybe could have done differently or some of the things he did well and it just wasn't his night.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on sports media: I always thought there was too much negativity in scrutinizing players. I do not need to go on TV and tell everybody that the guy who went three for 17 sucks at basketball. He does not. He had an off night.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on developing his game while maintaining his strengths
quotes.excerpt: Use your athleticism, get to the rim, put pressure on the rim, and then let that be
quotes.quote: Use your athleticism, get to the rim, put pressure on the rim, and then let that be your playmaking. Because now people have to rotate over, they have to help. Now you can open up different parts of your game. A lot of times players hear, he can't do this, he can't do that, and sometimes you block out what you do well and you're so focused on what people are saying you can't do.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on development: Use your athleticism, get to the rim, put pressure on the rim, and then let that be your playmaking. A lot of times players hear what they cannot do and block out what they actually do well.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on his transition to an analytical view of basketball
quotes.excerpt: I'm interested a little bit more in the chess match that's happening.
quotes.quote: I'm interested a little bit more in the chess match that's happening. Trying to analyze, you're looking, okay, what's the matchups? What would I have maybe done differently in that matchup? What could they do differently? What worked, what didn't work? And then you're watching both sides of the ball.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his analytical approach to the game: I am interested in the chess match. Trying to analyze the matchups, what would I have done differently, what worked and what did not work.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on why he decided to retire
quotes.excerpt: I still enjoyed the game of basketball, but I was enjoying less and less everything else that
quotes.quote: I still enjoyed the game of basketball, but I was enjoying less and less everything else that came with it. For one, my last several years I was in Michigan, Detroit, I was in Brooklyn, I was in Boston, and my kids are in school here. So being away from them was tough. Even getting to see them once a month is still a little bit brutal.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his decision to retire: I still enjoyed the game of basketball, but I was enjoying less and less everything else that came with it. Being away from my kids was tough. Even seeing them once a month is still a little bit brutal.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on JJ Redick's advice regarding retirement
quotes.excerpt: You won't be truly happy until you retire.
quotes.quote: I remember I was playing golf with JJ Redick once before I retired, and he said something to me that stuck with me. He was like, I'm telling you, you won't be truly happy until you retire.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin shares the advice JJ Redick gave him before he retired: I am telling you, you will not be truly happy until you retire.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on his 2017 playoff injury
quotes.excerpt: I tore a ligament on the bottom of my foot in the playoffs in 2017.
quotes.quote: I tore a ligament on the bottom of my foot in the playoffs in 2017. That season, I had a chef to make sure all my meals were exactly what I needed. I slept, I took my pre-game naps in a hyperbaric chamber, I would nap in a hyperbaric chamber on off days, ice baths, hot tub, hot cold, sauna. I was doing everything possible. And I remember the doctor coming in telling me that I tore my tendon and I had to have surgery, and I just broke down.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on the 2017 playoff injury that broke him: I was doing everything possible. I slept in a hyperbaric chamber, I had a chef. And I remember the doctor telling me I tore my tendon and had to have surgery, and I just broke down.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on Chris Paul's influence on his game
quotes.excerpt: Chris Paul always talking to me about screening angles and the strategy of how he wants to
quotes.quote: Chris Paul always talking to me about screening angles and the strategy of how he wants to screen or what I should be doing. It's not that I wasn't hearing that, but you couldn't quite grasp it until you get it. And as an older player, you start to understand these things better and they become second nature, so you're not having to think through everything.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on Chris Paul: Chris Paul always talked to me about screening angles and the strategy of how he wants to screen. As an older player, you start to understand these things better and they become second nature.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on the inspiration behind his show 'The Step Back'
quotes.excerpt: I had this idea for the show a long time ago. I was watching John Oliver.
quotes.quote: I had this idea for the show a long time ago. I was watching John Oliver in 2016, and John Oliver is like the way I'd make sense of real-world issues, politics, whatever is going on. And it also keeps me entertained and locked in with the comedy aspect. I was always watching these reactionary debate shows, morning TV on basketball or sports in general, and realizing that there's sort of a void of sports entertainment where you feel like you're learning about some of these bigger issues that affect fans, sports fans, athletes, and even, honestly, not fans.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his show The Step Back: I was watching these reactionary debate shows and realizing there is a void of sports entertainment where you feel like you are learning about bigger issues that affect fans and athletes.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on his criticism of Stephen A. Smith
quotes.excerpt: I got a bone to pick with Stephen A. Smith.
quotes.quote: I got a bone to pick with Stephen A. Smith, and going at it from my perspective, just my perspective.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on Stephen A. Smith: I got a bone to pick with Stephen A. Smith, and going at it from my perspective.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on the debate culture in sports media
quotes.excerpt: Stephen A. Smith and Skip screaming about it, screaming at each other.
quotes.quote: We were sitting in the training room one time and First Take was on, and it was like Stephen A. Smith and Skip screaming about it, screaming at each other, and the topic was our team. And we're sitting in there just like, some guys were like not paying attention, but guys were like dying laughing because they're both just dead wrong. It's not like one guy is, you're like, oh, he's got a good point there. You're like, what are they talking about?
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on First Take: We were in the training room and Stephen A. Smith and Skip were screaming about our team. Guys were dying laughing because they were both just dead wrong. You are like, what are they talking about?

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on being traded via Twitter
quotes.excerpt: I didn't even process it when I first saw it.
quotes.quote: I didn't even process it when I first saw it. It was like, I we'd had this free agency meeting with just the front office and myself, my agent, my brother, and we come down stairs in Staples Center, Staples at the time, and a lot of the staff is around and they all have these shirts on, and I'm just saying hi. I mean, it's people that I've known for nine years or eight years at the time. I was just saying hi and I kind of clocked the shirt, but I didn't like, I didn't start looking at each person being like, wait, why are, why did we do this? And I kid you not, I said hello to everybody, got in the car, was on the 10 driving home, and the picture of the shirt was everywhere.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on finding out he was traded: I said hello to everybody, got in the car, was on the 10 driving home, and the picture of the shirt was everywhere.

quotes.speaker: Blake Griffin
quotes.summary_phrase: Blake Griffin on his pride in his time with the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I look back with a sense of pride. I think with the organization, when I got drafted
quotes.quote: I look back with a sense of pride. I think with the organization, when I got drafted to the Clippers, owned by Donald Sterling, who we touched on, historically bad franchise. It was a punchline. And over the course of, you know, eight years of being there, we got Chris Paul, we got JJ, we got DeAndre, we got all these guys and we were making runs at, you know, not only just getting to the playoffs, but certain years I felt like we had a legitimate chance to to win a championship. And obviously, ultimately came short, but I look back on it with a sense of pride.
quotes.social_post: Blake Griffin on his Clippers tenure: When I got drafted, it was a punchline. Over eight years, we got Chris Paul, JJ, DeAndre, and we had a legitimate chance to win a championship. I look back on it with a sense of pride.
